text:
maya: Quick bug report on the uploads docs. The API reference shows the request body as JSON/base64 only, but our hosted endpoint expects multipart/form-data. I tried the example and got HTTP 415.

maya: Example in PR (broken for hosted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"filename":"pic.png","file":"<base64>"}'
```

ryan: Oof. Thanks for catching. We should make multipart the primary example and keep the JSON/base64 as an alternate for Dedicated/on-prem only.

leah: Agreed. Also our SDK helpers abstract this away so we should add short SDK examples (py/js/go) that show the convenience call instead of manual form-data construction.

sanjay: Clarifying runtime constraints: hosted = multipart/form-data only. Dedicated/private may accept base64 JSON if the deployment has the legacy_uploads toggle enabled. We need a clear note in the ref and migration doc.

maya: Proposed changes:
- Update OpenAPI requestBody to accept both media types, but document multipart as the canonical hosted contract.
- Swap the JSON cURL snippet for multipart cURL + python requests + go http examples.
- Add a bold callout: "Hosted API requires multipart/form-data for uploads. JSON/base64 is legacy and only available on Dedicated/Private with legacy_uploads enabled."

ryan: I'll update the PR. Plan: OpenAPI -> requestBody oneOf [multipart/form-data, application/json], examples under each media type; main page shows multipart first. Also will add a short migration note.

ryan: New cURL multipart example I'll add:
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -F "file=@./pic.png" 
  -F "filename=pic.png"
# curl sets Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=... automatically
```

leah: Nice. For the docs render, call out max file size for hosted (25 MB) and show a server error example when >25MB. Also mention retries/backoff for 413/429 cases.

sanjay: Confirmed hosted max: 25 MB. Dedicated installs can be configured per-customer. Add that detail.

maya: SDK snippets to include (short):
Python:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY'))
res = c.upload_file(path='pic.png', filename='pic.png')
print(res['id'])
```
Go (http client example):
```go
file, _ := os.Open("pic.png")
body := &bytes.Buffer{}
writer := multipart.NewWriter(body)
part, _ := writer.CreateFormFile("file", "pic.png")
io.Copy(part, file)
writer.WriteField("filename", "pic.png")
writer.Close()
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads", body)
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
req.Header.Set("Content-Type", writer.FormDataContentType())
client.Do(req)
```

ryan: I'll also add a small table in the reference: payload type | supported on Hosted | supported on Dedicated | notes. Then move the base64 example to an "Alternate payloads" box.

_docs-preview-bot: Preview for PR 934 deployed: https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/pr/934/uploads-multipart-first — check examples and the alternate payload callout._

leah: Preview looks good. One nit: the Go example rendered with long lines, add a short note about streaming large files instead of reading all into memory.

maya: Good point, I'll add a streaming example snippet and the file-size note. Assigning reviews: ryan (author), sanjay (technical), leah (docs). Will merge after approvals.

ryan: Thanks all, will push the branch and update the PR description. :thumbsup:
